skill.name: nanobanana
skill.description: Generate, edit, restore, and specialize images with Google's Gemini image models through a self-contained Python CLI.
skill.summary: Creates Gemini image outputs for prompts, edits, restoration, icons, patterns, diagrams, and story frames.
skill.author: batou9150

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are Markdown examples, placeholder environment variable names, or safe wrapper behavior. One critical pipe-to-shell installer was confirmed, and semantic review found runtime dependency, file selection, and secret storage risks.

remediation.issue: Remote installer is piped directly into the shell.
remediation.suggestion: Replace the curl pipe-to-shell instruction with package manager steps or a download, verify, then execute workflow.

remediation.issue: Runtime dependency resolution uses an unpinned google-genai range.
remediation.suggestion: Pin the dependency to an exact version and publish a lockfile or hash-verified install path.

remediation.issue: Edit and restore search personal folders before uploading an image.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit paths or limit lookup to the current workspace. Warn before using Downloads or Desktop files.

remediation.issue: Documentation recommends broad plaintext API key storage.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer scoped environment injection or a secret manager. Include file permission guidance when plaintext storage is unavoidable.

semantic_findings.title: Runtime Dependency Fetch Without Lockfile
semantic_findings.description: The script runs through uv run --script and declares google-genai>=1.0.0 without a lockfile. First use can fetch newer package code from the network.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The shebang and PEP 723 metadata directly show uv runtime dependency resolution. No pinned version or lockfile evidence was found.

semantic_findings.title: Broad Local File Search Before Upload
semantic_findings.description: Edit and restore commands search cwd, images, input, output, Downloads, and Desktop. The selected image bytes are then sent to the Gemini model.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code lists home-directory search paths and reads the selected file into the model request. This is intended behavior but can expose the wrong local image.

semantic_findings.title: Plaintext Shell-Wide Secret Storage Guidance
semantic_findings.description: The README recommends appending an API key to ~/.zshenv and notes that the file loads for every zsh invocation. This broadens secret exposure.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The setup instructions explicitly place a placeholder API key in shell or Claude settings files. The README itself notes plain text storage.

content.user_title: Create Gemini Images with Nano Banana
content.value_statement: Teams often need quick visual assets without leaving their AI workflow. This skill turns prompts and selected images into Gemini generated files for design, documentation, and product work.
actual_capabilities: Generate one or more images from a text prompt with count, style, and variation options.
Edit or restore a local image by sending the selected file and prompt to Gemini.
Create app icons, favicons, UI elements, patterns, textures, wallpapers, diagrams, and story frames.
Save generated image files into a nanobanana-output directory and print the paths.
Load reference guides for styles, prompt recipes, and troubleshooting when needed.
limitations: Requires uv, network access, and a Gemini compatible API key.
Image prompts and selected input images are sent to Google's Gemini service.
Generated image quality depends on the remote model response.
Preview mode depends on the operating system image opener.

use_cases.title: Produce Product Visuals
use_cases.description: Create icon sets, product mockups, and image variations for early design review.

use_cases.title: Improve Documentation Assets
use_cases.description: Generate diagrams, process frames, and visual explanations for technical guides.

use_cases.title: Repair or Adapt Images
use_cases.description: Restore damaged images or edit existing files for presentations and support materials.

prompt_templates.title: Generate a Simple Image
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate a clean watercolor image of a mountain lake at sunrise. Save the result and return the file path.

prompt_templates.title: Create Icon Assets
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a modern app icon for a budgeting app. Use a transparent background and produce 256 and 512 pixel outputs.

prompt_templates.title: Edit a Local Image
prompt_templates.prompt: Edit product-photo.png to remove background clutter and make the product ready for a marketplace listing.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Visual System
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a five frame process story showing seed germination. Keep the style consistent and save each frame separately.

output_examples.input: Create a favicon set for a mountain travel app.
output_examples.output: Returns saved paths for 16, 32, and 64 pixel favicon images in the output directory.

output_examples.input: Restore this scanned family photo and improve contrast.
output_examples.output: Returns one enhanced image with repaired damage, clearer contrast, and the saved file path.

output_examples.input: Draw an architecture diagram for a chat system.
output_examples.output: Returns a labeled technical diagram image showing services, data stores, queues, and monitoring.

best_practices: Use explicit file paths when editing or restoring images.
State the desired style, size, count, and output purpose in the prompt.
Review generated images before using them in public materials.
anti_patterns: Do not send sensitive personal images unless external model processing is acceptable.
Do not rely on preview mode in headless or remote environments.
Do not store broad API keys in shell startup files without access controls.

faq.question: What API key does this skill need?
faq.answer: It needs a Gemini compatible API key, preferably provided through NANOBANANA_API_KEY.

faq.question: Can it edit existing images?
faq.answer: Yes. The edit and restore commands read a selected local image and send it with the prompt.

faq.question: Where are generated files saved?
faq.answer: Generated images are saved in a nanobanana-output directory under the current working directory.

faq.question: Does it work without network access?
faq.answer: No. It calls Gemini image models and may resolve Python dependencies on first use.

faq.question: Can it create diagrams?
faq.answer: Yes. The diagram command supports flowchart, architecture, network, database, wireframe, mindmap, and sequence diagram prompts.

faq.question: Is it safe for private images?
faq.answer: Use caution. Selected input images are sent to Google for model processing.
